claim: Membrane fusion is required for TANGO1-dependent export of procollagen VII from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: Previously we showed that membrane fusion is required for TANGO1-dependent export of procollagen VII from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Nogueira, et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Nogueira, et al., 2014)

claim: The complete complement of SNAREs required for procollagen VII export includes t-SNAREs Syntaxin 18, BNIP1, and USE1, and v-SNARE YKT6.
source: Along with the t-SNARE Syntaxin 18, we now reveal the complete complement of SNAREs required in this process, t-SNAREs BNIP1 and USE1, and v-SNARE YKT6.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing knockdown effects

claim: TANGO1 recruits YKT6-containing ER Golgi Intermediate Compartment (ERGIC) membranes to procollagen VII-enriched patches on the ER.
source: TANGO1 recruits YKT6-containing ER Golgi Intermediate Compartment (ERGIC) membranes to procollagen VII-enriched patches on the ER.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing colocalization and recruitment assays

claim: Residues 1214-1396 of TANGO1, which include the first coiled coil, specifically recruit ERGIC membranes even when targeted to mitochondria.
source: Moreover residues 1214-1396, that include the first coiled coil of TANGO1, specifically recruit ERGIC membranes even when targeted to mitochondria.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing mitochondrial targeting experiments

claim: Growth of a mega transport carrier for collagen export from the ER occurs by addition of ERGIC membranes to procollagen-enriched domains of the ER, not by acquisition of a larger patch of ER membrane.
source: Our data reveal that growth of a mega transport carrier for collagen export from the ER is not by acquisition of a larger patch of ER membrane, but instead by addition of ERGIC membranes to procollagen-enriched domains of the ER by a TANGO1-mediated process.
evidence: Supported by experimental data and inference from the results presented

claim: Human cells express 28 collagens, most of which are secreted, constituting roughly 25% of dry body weight.
source: Human cells express 28 collagens, most of which are secreted, constituting roughly 25% of our dry body weight (Kadler et al., 2007; Malhotra et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature

claim: Procollagens contain rigid, rod-like triple-helical domains that can reach 450 nm in length.
source: A challenge arises from the fact that procollagens contain rigid, rod-like triple-helical domains that can reach 450 nm in length (Burgeson et al., 1985)
evidence: Supported by citation to established literature

claim: Procollagens are too large to be exported from the ER by conventional COPII-coated vesicles of 60–90 nm diameter.
source: procollagens contain rigid, rod-like triple-helical domains that can reach 450 nm in length (Burgeson et al., 1985) and are too large to be exported from the ER by conventional COPII (Coat Protein complex II)-coated vesicles of 60–90 nm diameter (Glick and Malhotra, 1998; Malhotra et al., 2015; Miller and Schekman, 2013; Saito and Katada, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations and logical inference from size comparison

claim: TANGO1 is an ER-exit site resident protein.
source: An important first step in addressing the mechanism of procollagen export from the ER was the identification of an ER-exit site resident protein called TANGO1 (Bard et al., 2006; Saito et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The SH3-like domain of TANGO1 is required for its binding to procollagen VII in the ER lumen.

evidence: Supported by established knowledge from previous studies

claim: The second coiled coil domain of TANGO1 binds a protein called cTAGE5.

evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The C-terminal proline rich domains (PRD's) of TANGO1 and cTAGE5 interact with the COPII coat proteins Sec23A and Sec24C.

claim: TANGO1 mediates export of the only collagen expressed and secreted by Drosophila.

claim: TANGO1 knockout mice are defective in the sorting and export of many collagens.

claim: CC-TMCC3 localises to the ER.

claim: TEER is sufficient to recruit ERGIC membranes to the ER.

claim: Mit-CC-TMCC3 localises to mitochondria.

claim: Mit-TEER and Mit-CC-TMCC3 are inserted into outer mitochondrial membranes and are exposed to the cytoplasm.
source: Both Mit-TEER and Mit-CC-TMCC3 were degraded upon incubation of membranes with proteinase K in the absence of detergent; in contrast, ATP5A1, a subunit of the mitochondrial inner membrane-localised ATP synthase, was intact under the same conditions. As expected, inclusion of detergent further led to the degradation of ATP5A1 by proteinase K (Figure 4D). These data show that Mit-TEER and Mit-CC-TMCC3 are inserted into outer mitochondrial membranes and are exposed to the cytoplasm.

claim: HeLa cells expressing Mit-TEER, but not Mit-CC-TMCC3, recruited ERGIC-53-containing membranes to mitochondria.
